solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: the dispute sits inside the currency, so one word is placed within the other

parts.note: the sen was a Japanese coin, a hundredth of a yen
a tiff is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: An economist proposes shoring up the yen amid a row.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something stiff is to make it firmer, a direct synonym for strengthening it.

parts.note: to spar is to argue or box, so spars means disputes
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: Lovers' quarrels are said to be uncommon with a darling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' is read as 'the heart of sweet', its central letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse and rare both describe something thinly scattered or scarce.

clue.text: I am a long time getting the likeness

parts.note: contracted, I am is I'm
an age is a very long period

explanation.surface: Someone ages over the years while sitting for a portrait.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a representation or likeness of someone, as in a picture.

clue.text: Feels a bit irritated by trifling annoyances

indicators.note: letters that are irritated are stirred up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone feels slightly itchy from minor insect bites.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleabites are literally tiny bites, and figuratively minor irritations or trifles.

parts.note: turning over a fresh page signals reform, and in spring trees literally put out fresh foliage

explanation.surface: A penitent's symbol appears in springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning over a new leaf is the idiom for reforming one's ways; spring brings new leaves on trees.

clue.text: Give a hand when son is on time

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'
S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies

explanation.surface: A son helps out by arriving punctually.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist is to help, or lend a hand.

clue.text: In the bay wrecked ship sunk deep

indicators.note: wrecked letters are broken up and put back in a new order

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A wrecked vessel lies sunk at the bottom of the bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sunk' and 'In the' only join the surface; 'deep' is a noun, the abyss.
explanation.definitionFit: The deep is the profound ocean, and an abyss is a bottomless depth.

parts.note: a guy is also an effigy, like the figure of Guy Fawkes, and this one stands among the crops

explanation.surface: A man is spotted standing out in a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure dressed as a man stands in fields to frighten birds: a guy in the effigy sense.

clue.text: Cast Pete in play and watch

indicators.note: letters put in play are moved about freely into a new order

explanation.surface: An actor named Pete is cast in a show, and others come to see it.
explanation.definitionFit: To spectate is to be an onlooker, simply to watch an event.

clue.text: It holds wine for a service in church

indicators.note: the service sits inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
the RAF, Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A vessel of communion wine is used during a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A carafe is a glass flask for serving wine or water at table.

indicators.note: the scrambled word goes around the food, enclosing it
terribly signals the word wary is jumbled

parts.note: fare means food, as in a bill of fare

explanation.surface: A hiker is very cautious about what they eat on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' turns WARY into WAYR, which 'about' wraps round FARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A wayfarer is one who journeys on foot, a traveller.

clue.text: Blameless in disorder, left out from group

indicators.note: in disorder says the remaining letters are jumbled
left out means the abbreviation for left is dropped from the word

explanation.surface: An innocent party is excluded from a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' takes one L from BLAMELESS, giving BAMELESS (or BLAMEESS), which 'in disorder' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To group things is to gather them together, the verb sense of assemble.

indicators.note: the wrong arrangement means the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone has picked up the wrong suitcase.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath is a close-fitting cover or case, as for a knife or sword.

definitions.meaning: with the bottles of spirits all drunk

explanation.definitionFit: Spirits means both mood and strong liquor, so being without them is gloom or an empty bar.

parts.note: read not as 'amply full' but as a ship filled from a well, an oil well

explanation.surface: A container is brimming over.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship carrying crude pumped from oil wells is a vessel filled from a well.

clue.text: Set up strike — a rise is most important

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word is written upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to rap is to strike sharply
to mount is to rise or climb

explanation.surface: A strike is organised and a pay rise is the top priority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' turns RAP into PAR in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramount means supreme, of chief importance.

definitions.meaning: the closing of a reactor or plant
a stoppage of work by employees

explanation.definitionFit: A shutdown is the stopping of a reactor, and also the halting of work in industrial action.

clue.text: Starts out in our police force, it's back-breaking!

indicators.note: the jumbled word goes inside the police force

parts.note: the law is a colloquial name for the police

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A new recruit joins the force and finds it all too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns STARTS into STSTRA, which 'in' places within THE LAW. The definition refers to the straw that breaks the camel's back.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial final burden breaks the camel's back, so it is fittingly back-breaking.

indicators.note: cryptic means obscured, so the word clues is scrambled
pointless says a compass point, here E for east, is removed

explanation.surface: A solver complains that cryptic clues are a waste of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic' gives SECUL from CLUES; 'pointless' drops E (east, a compass point) from ARE, leaving AR.
explanation.definitionFit: Secular means worldly rather than spiritual, hence mundane in its old sense.

clue.text: Festivities involve five in lively dances

indicators.note: the dances involve, or contain, the numeral

parts.note: reels are brisk Scottish dances
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A party features five energetic dances.
explanation.definitionFit: Revels are lively celebrations, festivities.

parts.note: suggests dangerous creatures let loose, but means lost pets wandering without a lead

explanation.surface: Wild beasts are being set loose upon the public.
explanation.definitionFit: Stray dogs and cats roam without an owner or leash, loose among the community.

clue.text: Doubtful, being kept somewhat in the dark?

definitions.text: being kept somewhat in the dark?
definitions.meaning: partly out of the light, in the shade

explanation.definitionFit: Shady describes both something dubious or disreputable and a place out of direct sunlight.

parts.note: sounds like an athlete's exercise routine, but means someone who catches the train every morning

explanation.surface: A fitness fanatic exercises each morning before the office.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who travels daily by rail to their workplace is literally taking trains before work.

definitions.meaning: a surprise win by an underdog

explanation.definitionFit: Upset means knocked over, and in sport a shock result where the favourite loses.

clue.text: Drink to the end of the rooster?

explanation.definitionFit: A mixed drink shares its name with the tail feathers of a cock, the male fowl.

indicators.note: an unexpected arrangement turns the letters of the word into a surprise order

explanation.surface: Home rule for Ireland had an outcome no one foresaw.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Stewart Parnell led the 19th-century campaign for Irish Home Rule, which provoked fierce resistance in the northern province, an outcome he did not plan for.
explanation.definitionFit: The northern Irish province resisted Home Rule, the surprising consequence of the nationalist campaign.

clue.text: You start on green — get set — go!

indicators.note: the letters get set, placed in a new arrangement
start means the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A starter tells a runner the lights are green: ready, steady, go!
explanation.walkthrough: 'get set' rearranges GREEN; 'You start' gives Y, placed 'on' (after) it.
explanation.definitionFit: Go means vigour or drive, as in 'full of go', a synonym of energy.

indicators.note: about signals the letters are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone turns round to gawp.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotates means spins or turns about an axis.
